answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy makes fake identities expensive and real ones cheap to verify. A quartz-hard stake forces every agent to lock collateral slashed on fraud, so minting 10,000 sock puppets costs 10,000 stakes. Reputation climbs a ridge: new agents earn almost nothing until sustained honest work proves them, so a farm burns months of compute before extracting value. Each task is signed with a quill only the agent key can wield, binding rewards to verifiable history, not a free username. Attackers pay capital, time and compute per identity; honest agents pay only good behavior.
